stem.en: Phlogiston explained why a candle in a jar goes out: the air "fills up" with phlogiston. What is the oxygen explanation for the same fact?

text.en: The candle uses up the oxygen in the jar, and with no oxygen left it cannot burn.

feedback.en: A candle burns happily in a hot kitchen. The jar run shows the flame dying while the jar is still barely warm.
A clean-burning candle makes almost no smoke and still goes out in a jar.

text.en: The candle runs out of wax.

feedback.en: The candle in the jar goes out with plenty of wax left. Relight it in open air and it burns on.

explanation.en: Both stories fit "the flame goes out". Only one fits "the metal gets heavier". Phlogiston could not survive the balance.
